pass_a_gloss: Rem mid continues mid word on prophecy: one prophecy that has gone beyond and one that has ascended. The more catholic kind imitating Isaiah and Jeremiah is second rank after apostleship; the last ranked kind after the named gifts is the congregational exposing prophecy of 1 Cor 14:24–25, close to workings of powers and healings that amaze onlookers, so the prophet can name what is in the heart and from what sin the person came to church. That prophecy can be later in order than the former; the more divine greater prophecy is the ‘second’ of ‘first apostles, second prophets, third teachers.’ To prove two senses of ‘prophecy,’ Origen restates: not all are apostles (else to whom is apostleship ministered?); not all are prophets in the high sense; yet ‘if you all prophesy’ treats the lower exposing prophecy as possible for all. Hence two significations; the apostle’s order first apostles second prophets is kept. So much on order, since ‘to another prophecy’ listed last elsewhere seemed to squeeze us. Fragment 49 on the more excellent way and tongues/prophecy/knowledge/faith without love: can anyone in this life have prophecy and all mysteries without love, and is knowing all mysteries even given? Paul says if anyone thinks he knows, he does not yet know as he must; we know and prophesy in part until the perfect comes. Spoken of himself and similar apostles, this shows knowing all mysteries and all knowledge is impossible. Why then speak as if possible? Look at the preface ‘I show a way according to hyperbole’ and grasp what hyperbole is. Greeks define hyperbole as speech overshooting truth for emphasis: whiter than snow; horses run like wind; Psalm waves to heavens and abysses; Deuteronomy cities walled to heaven—impossible yet emphatic. Likewise Paul takes a hypothesis to examine gift nature and love nature—not that so great a gift can exist without love, or full knowledge without love, or mountain moving faith—but to show love’s weight if set on a scale under a hypothetical speech. Therefore pursue love especially. Cut ends asking about angels— Origen further notes that the exposing prophecy can declare the entrant’s hidden sin and still stand later in gift order than apostleship linked prophecy.  The dual sense alone rescues Paul’s seemingly jumbled lists. Hyperbole examples from snow, wind swift horses, psalm waves, and heaven high walls all train the reader not to take the ‘all knowledge / all faith without love’ case as a real attainable state in this life, but as a weighing device that elevates love over every charism.
pass_b_english: —prophecy that has surpassed and a prophecy that has gone up. He will call the more catholic sort, imitating the prophecies of Isaiah and Jeremiah, second rank after the apostleship; but this last-ranked sort after the gifts already named is such as: [[if you prophesy, and an unbeliever or ungifted person comes in, he is convicted by all, examined by all, the secrets of his heart become plain, and so falling on his face he will worship God and announce that God is truly among you >> Bible:1 Corinthians 14:24-25]]. For this is not far from the working of powers and the gift of healings that happen for the amazement of those who see, so that the one prophesying may say, “You have this in your heart; from this sin you have come to the church.” This prophecy can also be later in rank than the former ones, while that more divine and greater one is second, of which he says, [[God set in the church first apostles, second prophets, third teachers >> Bible:1 Corinthians 12:28]].

To establish that two things are signified from the name “prophecy,” I set out beforehand what I said. See whether I can still show the saying more clearly: God set in the church first apostles—but not all are apostles; for if all were apostles, to whom would they minister the apostleship? Second, prophets—not all are prophets; yet according to the other prophecy, “if you all prophesy, and an unbeliever or ungifted person comes in,” it is spoken not as of an impossibility but as of a possibility that all prophesy in that way. So there are two significations from the name “prophecy.” Therefore here too the apostle’s order is kept that says first apostles, second prophets, and the rest. So much concerning the order, since the phrase “to another prophecy,” ranked last in another wording, seemed to press us.

49 on [[1 Corinthians 13:1–2 >> Bible:1 Corinthians 13:1-2]]: “And I show you a still more excellent way. If I speak with the tongues of humans and of angels, but do not have love, I have become a sounding bronze or a clanging cymbal. And if I have prophecy and know all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have all faith so as to move mountains, but do not have love, I am nothing.” [Origen:] We ask here whether someone in this life can both have prophecy and know all the mysteries without love, and altogether whether it is given to anyone to know all mysteries; for Paul says, [[If anyone thinks he has come to know something, he does not yet know as he ought to know >> Bible:1 Corinthians 8:2]]; and again, [[we know in part and we prophesy in part; but when the perfect comes, the partial will be done away >> Bible:1 Corinthians 13:9-10]]. Saying these things about himself and the apostles like him shows that it is not possible to know all mysteries and all knowledge. How then does he speak as if it were possible to know all knowledge and understand all mysteries?

If we look at the preface of the words, in which he says, “And I show you a still more excellent way,” and understand what “excellence” (hyperbole) is, all this will be clarified. Hyperbole, then, as even the Greeks defined it, is speech that for the sake of emphasis overshoots the truth; and they use the example that some are said to be whiter than snow—not that anything can be whiter than snow, but it is said by hyperbole. And again: some horses run like wind—not that such a thing is possible, but for emphasis, so that the horses’ speed may be shown, such a thing is said of them. And in the Scripture of the Psalms it is said of the sea, [[their waves go up to the heavens and go down to the abysses >> Bible:Psalm 107:26]]—which is impossible, but said for emphasis. And in the law you will find the manner of hyperbole written where it is written, [[We saw cities great and walled up to heaven >> Bible:Deuteronomy 1:28]]. How can this be? Yet it is said hyperbolically, the speech not altogether presenting the thing signified itself but showing the greatness of the waves or the lowliness, and the greatness of the walls, or something near these.

So also here the apostle takes a hypothesis in order that the nature of gifts and the nature of love may be examined—not that it is possible for a gift, and so great a gift, to exist without love; or that it is possible in this life for someone to know all knowledge without love, or to have such faith as to move mountains; but wanting to show that if love were set in a balance—the word being spoken by hypothesis. He says, then, that one must especially zealously pursue love. Do angels—
